title: I made an ASCII world sim that runs history while you're away. Same seed, 10,000 ticks, byte-identical every time.
author: lerugray
selftext:
Veridian Contraption is a terminal world simulator in Rust. A colored ASCII map sits on the left and a chronicle scrolls on the right. Civilizations found guilds, run show trials, march levies and get hit by one of seven Eschatons, catastrophes that reshape the map for good without ending the world. You leave it running, come back, and read what happened.

What you can do besides watch:

- **Adventure mode.** Step into the running world as one adventurer, a real agent in the same sim. Take bounties off settlement petition boards, recruit companions who have their own lives, fight turn-based Clashes, and walk dungeons. Retire to a roster and your adventurer keeps living there, or die for good and get an epitaph built from your own chronicle.
- **The Bureau Advisor.** Each world generates a counselor with a personality and an ASCII portrait. It comments on wars, famines, deaths and Eschatons as they happen.
- **Patron actions.** Sponsor artists, start rumors, declare trade embargoes, seed rivalries, grant titles. You can also found your own guild, cult or mercenary company, fund it, and commission quests from a patron budget.
- **Magic.** Six traditions, including Bureaucromancer. Wizard towers, corruption, and rogue wizards.
- **Off-map powers.** Foreign forces show up as rumors, then sightings, then arrive to invade, parley or settle, sometimes with multi-phase sieges.

How it was built: Claude Code wrote the code. I design board wargames for a living, so I did the design: 170+ event types, five prose registers for the chronicle (Clinical, Lyrical, Bureaucratic, Ominous, Conspiratorial), and a tabletop-style combat results table for wars. A task file and a short mission doc in the repo meant each session started from the same page.

The one thing worth stealing: every change had to pass a determinism test. Run the same seed for 10,000 ticks twice and diff the output byte for byte. It caught more agent regressions than anything else I tried. If you build a sim with an agent, set that up on day one. (I later added 25k and 50k versions, plus a check that saving at 5,000 and resuming lands on the same bytes as a straight run.)

The art and the 14-track score aren't AI. They're instrumentals I recorded over the years, picked to sit under the text. I do music for games too; the trailer has a sample. The soundtrack is a free download with the game.

Trailer: https://youtu.be/Kc0vFZs8qM8
itch: https://conflict-simulations-llc.itch.io/veridian-contraption

Question for people building sims: how do you keep an agent from quietly breaking determinism? Seed diffs are my only guard so far.
